outroLine: Your columns, your format — parsed as-is.

beats.shot: Land on /upload; cursor traces the accepted-format line; a real CSV is dropped — 'Detected: CSV' appears.
beats.vo: C S V and X L S X are the two most common ways an order arrives, and both parse the same way. Row one is the header, every row after it is a line — and headers are matched by name, never by position.

beats.shot: Code overlay: the dropped CSV's text with the header row highlighted; header fields read from the first row that carries a value.
beats.vo: There's no rigid template, and nothing in the file is strictly required — a recognisable header row and one line is enough. Anything missing is defaulted or left open for review, and header fields like P O number, date, buyer and currency are read from the first row that carries a value.

beats.shot: Code overlay: 'Buyer Item Code', 'buyerItemCode' and 'BUYER_ITEM_CODE' all normalising to the same field; an unknown column shown as ignored.
beats.vo: You don't have to rename your columns. ProcuLink lowercases each header and strips spaces and punctuation — so Buyer Item Code, written three different ways, resolves to the same field. And a column it doesn't recognise is simply ignored.

beats.shot: Code overlay: encoding behaviour — UTF-8 decode, BOM stripped, line endings normalised; a legacy Windows-codepage file garbles accents/€ (no auto-detection).
beats.vo: Files decode as UTF-8. A byte-order mark is stripped and line endings are normalised automatically. There is no legacy-codepage detection though — a file saved in an old Windows encoding can garble accents and the euro sign, so choose C S V UTF-8 when you export.

beats.shot: Code overlay: the number rules — both separators → last one is the decimal; semicolon-delimited = European signal; an ambiguous CSV number is flagged for review, never guessed.
beats.vo: Numbers are read locale-aware. When a value carries both a dot and a comma, the last one is the decimal separator — so European and U S styles both read correctly. A semicolon-delimited file is the reliable European signal. And when a C S V number is truly ambiguous, ProcuLink refuses to guess — that line is flagged for review instead of shipping a silently wrong value.

beats.shot: Overlay dismissed; supplier picked; 'Upload & review' clicked — the parsed order opens for review.
beats.vo: Then the parsed order opens for review, line by line. X L S X follows the same shape, read from the first worksheet — and it's an input format only. ProcuLink delivers back out in whatever format the supplier requires.
